name: Victoria Clara Swart — The Journal
description: Essays on brand strategy, language, psychology, and culture — the thinking behind how businesses are seen and remembered.

blogPost.headline: The Psychology of Positioning
blogPost.description: Why the way a brand is perceived matters as much — if not more — than what it delivers. On anchoring, context, and the invisible architecture of trust.
blogPost.keywords: brand positioning, brand psychology, brand strategy

blogPost.headline: Why Good Brands Sound Clear Before They Look Expensive
blogPost.description: Luxury is often misread as decoration. In communication, it is the opposite: restraint, precision, and the courage to say less.

blogPost.headline: What International Living Teaches You About Communication
blogPost.description: Having lived across five countries and spoken five languages professionally — the gap between fluency and actual understanding.

blogPost.headline: Taste, Trust, and Digital Presence
blogPost.description: The aesthetic choices a brand makes online signal far more than style. On visual decisions and perceived credibility.
blogPost.keywords: digital presence, brand credibility, web design

blogPost.headline: What Aviation Taught Me About Communication
blogPost.description: In aviation, ambiguity is a safety risk. The same principle applies to brand language — on clarity, protocols, and precision as respect.

blogPost.headline: Storytelling Beyond Marketing
blogPost.description: The most compelling brand narratives aren't built in campaign briefs. They come from knowing what a business genuinely stands for.
blogPost.keywords: brand storytelling, narrative strategy, content strategy
